Q192.reason: The friend agreed to help and drove the young man to the house intending the burglary to occur so he would be caught, so the agreement and the intent that the crime be committed are both present, which makes conspiracy the best fit.

Q193.reason: Under Plyler v. Doe, a fee that effectively bars children of undocumented aliens from public school is not substantially related to an important governmental interest, so the ordinance is invalid.

Q194.reason: The manufacturer failed to deliver 10 of the 500 contracted widgets, so the buyer can recover damages for that shortfall even though it accepted the other 490.
